subject: rstan failing to compile model that works in cmdstan

messages.author: 7b2fb40653accdcf
messages.subject: rstan failing to compile model that works in cmdstan
parts:
Hello,

I have model that runs in cmdstan, but fails in rstan, with the message documented in the screen capture.  (other times the same program fails with a message saying I cannot allocate a vector with 15.4 billion elements, other times rstudio hangs).

Full disclosure, I upgraded from Fedora 22 to 23 two days ago and reinstalled rstudio and rstan (using install.packages("rstan",type="source") and didn't notice any unusual messages.

The documentation is here:

https://github.com/equinn1/STAN_debug

If you need anything else, please let me know.

Best regards,

Gene Quinn

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: rstan failing to compile model that works in cmdstan
parts:
On Monday, February 29, 2016 at 3:18:56 PM UTC-5, Eugene Quinn wrote:
I have model that runs in cmdstan, but fails in rstan, with the message documented in the screen capture.  (other times the same program fails with a message saying I cannot allocate a vector with 15.4 billion elements, other times rstudio hangs).

It sounds as if R may just have ran out of RAM. There is now a save_warmup logical flag that you can pass to stan() or sampling(), which if FALSE will not save the warmup (which was historically the biggest runtime difference between CmdStan and RStan).

The "negative length vectors" thing has come up before, and may have to do with trying to internally pass a signed int to something expecting an unsigned int. It usually goes away if you have the latest Rcpp, RcppEigen, and rstan all using the same compiler.

Ben

messages.author: 7b2fb40653accdcf
messages.subject: Re: rstan failing to compile model that works in cmdstan
parts:
Thanks Ben,

I deleted and rebuilt Rcpp and RcppEigen from source and that fixed the problem.  I appreciate your help!

Gene Quinn
